title: Workflow Editor
subtitle: Create nodes and edges on the canvas and bind each node to a role and a model; right-click the canvas to add an end node.
selectHint: Select a node or edge on the canvas to configure it.
workflowControlsHelp: Max reject rounds limits failure loops (1-9, blank uses 9); heterogeneity sets dev/review model validation strength; onMaxRounds picks the over-limit behavior.
maxRoundsHelp: Each failure transition consumes one round; the workflow fails beyond the limit (system cap 9).
heteroCheckHelp: Model heterogeneity strength for dev/review nodes, saved with the blueprint. Weak (default): same provider with different models is allowed with a warning; identical provider+model is rejected. Strong: providers must differ. Off: no validation, identical models are an explicit user choice and are not flagged.
onMaxRoundsHelp: After max rounds: return=terminate; auto-reschedule=run failure attribution (attribution/split/human advice) then terminate.
fanoutItemsHelp: Use $.results.<node-id>.<field> or $.args.<field>; reference the current item as {{item}} in the goal.
fanoutFailOnHelp: any=one failure; all=all fail (default); number N=failedCount > N.
perItemSchemaHelp: This schema validates each sub-agent result, not the aggregate wrapper.
profileHelp: A profile maps to dsh/roles/<profile>.md in the workspace; its content is provided to the AI at runtime.
roleMgmtHint: Node config picks a role; this panel manages role assets.
roleFromSource: From "{src}"; saving creates an independent copy.
roleSummaryPlaceholder: e.g. Final verification against the agreed acceptance criteria.
roleSummaryHelp: The list shows only the summary; when left empty, two lines are taken from the duties.
roleContentPlaceholder: Describe the role positioning, duties, workflow and output requirements (Markdown).
roleContentHelp: Saved to dsh/roles/<role-name>.md in the workspace; the file content is given to the node AI at runtime.
roleNameInvalid: Role name is required, at most 64 chars, no illegal chars (/\:*?"<>|)
roleViewBuiltin: Built-in roles are system standard templates: read-only; you may view, select, or create a custom variant from one.
roleDeleteDesc: After deletion the role cannot be recovered or reused.
roleDeleteBlocked: "{name}" is still used by {n} node(s) and cannot be deleted. Switch those nodes to another role first, then delete after all references are gone.
roleRenameBlocked: This role is still used by {n} node(s); renaming would break those references. Remove the references first, or use "Create custom role from this role" to make a variant.
roleUsageConfirm: This role is used by {n} node(s); after saving, those positions will share the new configuration.
roleUsageFailed: Failed to read role usage; change not saved:
defaultNodeGoal: Describe what this node should accomplish.
resultModeDescription: AI output validation and manual check are mutually exclusive; enabling either one disables the other.
outputValidationDescription: Require the AI to return constrained JSON, then use the success expression to decide success or failure.
manualCheckDescription: The run pauses at this node (AWAITING_HUMAN) until a human decides success or failure.
resultModeRoutingDescription: Node output is routed by the outcomePath field: each exhaustible value maps to one business outcome edge (no success/failure verdict).
routingOutcomePathHelp: $.field form; the field must be declared in output.schema with exhaustible values (enum / const / boolean).
routingFieldNameHelp: The output field that decides where to go (e.g. route): whatever value the node's final output puts in this field selects the matching out-edge on the canvas. The value list below is the set of allowed values.
routingFieldNameHint: What it does: after the node runs, the value it outputs in this field decides which out-edge is taken (e.g. value pass takes the edge labelled pass).
routingValuesHelp: Each value maps to one business outcome edge: ✅ edge exists, ⚠️ no edge yet (click "Add edge"), ❗ more than one edge (the kernel allows only one).
routingEdgeDuplicated: This value has multiple edges (the kernel allows only one)
routingValuesEmpty: Add at least one value first; the kernel requires this field to be exhaustible.
routingNotEnumerable: This field is not exhaustible in the JSON output constraint (needs enum / const / oneOf constants / boolean) and cannot serve as a business result route.
routingBooleanUnsupported: Boolean routing fields have no value list for now; edit them directly in the JSON output constraint.
routingNeedFieldName: Enter the business result field name first, then you can add or remove values.
routingNameInvalid: A parameter name may contain letters, digits and underscores, and cannot start with a digit (e.g. route / need_test).
routingRemoveBlocked: This value still has a corresponding edge; handle that edge before removing it.
outputSchemaHelp: Define the final JSON shape for the AI (standard JSON Schema). Save validates that the success expression path exists in it.
artifactFilesHelp: Declare the formal deliverables this step should produce (a path relative to the working directory + format); saving creates a numbered archive that cannot be overwritten.
qualityCostEmpty: No attempt details yet (available after run completes)
noFormalArtifacts: No formal deliverables recorded for this run
outputSchemaInvalid: Invalid JSON; fix it before it is written to the workflow.
outputSchemaAutofilled: Basic JSON Schema generated and filled in. You can keep editing.
successConditionHelp: Define how the node is considered successful, e.g. $.result == true. Nested paths supported. Save validates the path exists in the JSON output constraint.
edgeWhenHelp: Only success edges may carry when ($.path == value). Multiple success out-edges must all carry when.
edgeTechnicalHelp: On technical failure the node retries itself; technical edges require a Business Outcome Routing node.
edgeOutcomeNameHelp: Must match an exhaustible value of the outcomePath field in the node's output.schema (e.g. PASS / BLOCKED).
edgeOutcomeNameSelectHelp: The source node declares a business result field; pick one of its values here (the kernel allows exactly one out-edge per value).
edgeOutcomeUsed: Used by another edge of the same node
edgeCountRoundHelp: Rollback consumes the auto-rollback budget via countRound; business outcome edges only.
validationDialogDescription: Fix these issues first. After closing, invalid fields are highlighted in red.
runModePrimary: Option 1 (recommended): run this template directly from the chat session.
runModeEnhanced: Option 2: click "Run" in the panel to execute it in one step. See the help docs for the underlying mechanics.
builtinReadonly: The built-in template cannot be deleted
modelOverrideHelp: Each node picks its own provider and model independently. "Default" uses the node preset; "overridden" uses your choice. Each dropdown's keep-default option shows its actual value. Structure is never modified.
modelOverrideEmpty: Override is empty: fill in Provider and Model for at least one node.
modelOverrideConfirmClear: Clear all model overrides for this template and restore built-in defaults?
noModels: No models configured on the host (vwf.models empty); provider/model fall back to text inputs.
connectHint: Drag from the right handle of a node onto a target node to connect
oneClickCheckHelp: Static validation + Preflight Probe (#74): minimal real calls against deduplicated model bindings; results show in the result bar at the top of this editor
oneClickCheckProbePending: Static validation passed. Preflight Probe (#74) is not shipped yet, so model availability / runnability cannot be verified here. Content changes and save still run static checks.
dashParallel: ⚠ {n} tasks finishing at the same time would interfere with each other; the system completes them one at a time. Handle each decision waiting on you one by one.
dashRunIdPlaceholder: Run ID (click an entry above to fill it in)
dashPickRun: Select or enter a run ID to see the details
dashRunNotFound: No record found for this run
dashSupersededFolded: Multiple executions of the same task are merged into one row; earlier executions stay readable in the detail.
dashNoMatch: No tasks match the current filters
dashIntegrityFailed: The record summary cannot be read right now; the list still shows the run as-is: {err}
dashNoLogical: This run has no task attribution (legacy record)
rdChainNote: Each node lists every attempt (including rework rounds); pick one to go back and see the result of that attempt.
rdChainOpenResult: View the result of that attempt →
rdSelectNodeHint: Pick a node from the directory above — only its result is shown here.
rdPrevRoundNote: This result predates the rework; the new round has not reached this step yet.
rdNotStartedNote: Results and records will be kept here once it runs.
rdReturnNone: No return comments were recorded for this attempt
rdAfterReturnNote: The upstream step picks up these comments and the result is submitted for review again.
rdNodeNotRun: This node has not run in this round yet
rdRecordsUnavailable: This step's result content cannot be read right now; only the basic information is shown below.
rdBusinessOutcomeNone: This node declares no business outcome path
rdFanoutIndependent: Subtasks complete independently and never overwrite each other's results.
rdFanoutWaiting: Synthesis is waiting: {n} subtasks are still unfinished
rdFanoutNoSub: This parallel group has no subtask records
rdFanoutWaitingNote: While subtasks are unfinished the synthesis node shows waiting instead of a finished result.
rdDecisionImpactNote: The run stays the same run: a new round is appended and control events are kept — no look-alike new task.
rdDecisionNotYetLocked: After submitting, buttons lock and show a resuming state to prevent double submission.
rdDecisionDt01: Submit path is blocked: decision ticket DT-01-ui-resume-attribution is still open, so the UI will not start a resume and will not show success. The parameters and field mapping below are handed to the session instead.
rdDecisionNoPackage: This run carries no decision package (decision_package is empty), so no options can be listed.
rdDecisionConsumed: This decision was already consumed (decision_id {id}); it is not submitted again.
rdBlockedModel: Change the provider / model this run uses
rdBlockedRestoreNote: Recovery creates a new archived version; earlier versions stay readable.
rdBlockedDt01: Recovery submit path is blocked: decision ticket DT-01-ui-resume-attribution is still open, so the UI will not start a resume and will not show success. The parameters and field mapping below are handed to the session instead.
rdBlockedNoProvider: The host returned no usable provider / model options, so the model override cannot be composed.
rdPausedGuidancePlaceholder: Add context so the next step can follow your judgement
rdPausedResumeDt01: Resume submit path is blocked: decision ticket DT-01-ui-resume-attribution is still open, so the UI will not start a resume. The parameters below are handed to the session instead.
rdPausedNote: Pause guidance is not a human business outcome and is never written as a business conclusion.
rdControlPauseNote: Pause takes effect at the next completed-node checkpoint; it does not abort the current attempt.
rdControlInterruptNote: Interrupt now skips the checkpoint: the current attempt stops immediately and is recorded as INTERRUPTED.
rdControlGuidanceNote: Guidance is available only while PAUSED and is submitted through vwf.run.control; it produces no business result.
rdControlResumeNote: Resume uses the existing wf_run resume semantics (resume_paused).
rdControlTerminal: This run is terminal ({state}); the control surface is unavailable.
rdWsNoRecord: This run has no workspace record
rdWsStaleNote: On read failure an unknown state is shown instead of treating a stale cache as current fact.
ctlPending: Control request sent, waiting to take effect
ctlConfirmInterrupt: Interrupt the current node Attempt? It will be recorded as INTERRUPTED (no formal success result) and the run enters PAUSED.
pausedResumeCmd: Resume (same logical run, new segment): wf_run { taskId: "{taskId}", templateId: "{tpl}", resume_paused: true }
pausedGuidanceCmd: Submit guidance (multi-round): wf_control { action: "guidance", logical_run_id: "{id}", text: "...", mode: "coach" }; for a real baseline change use mode: "baseline" plus required new_baseline
guidanceTimeline: Guidance Timeline (run-level, read-only; resumed nodes read all records)
probeForceRerunHint: Same probe: bypass the 5s cache and force real calls (results appear in the same place as One-click check)
probeNodeInherit: no model bound; inherits the session model at run time (no probe needed)
probeNodeNotProbed: not probed (the probe returned no verdict for this node)
probeNoBindings: No explicit model bindings; nothing to probe.
probeLlmUnavailable: llm service unavailable: cannot run the Preflight Probe. Make sure the llm service is mounted in the DSH host.
probeStatusInternalError: probe internal error (not a provider verdict)
modelOverrideConfirmDiscard: Unsaved override changes — discard and close?
nodeIdHelp: The node id is how expressions reference this step's result; changing it must be reflected everywhere it is referenced.
wbNoSteps: No steps yet — add a node on the canvas first.
wbConnDialogDesc: Every connection in this template, listed one by one: normal routing, business loops and call retries. Click a row to locate it on the canvas.
wbConnEmpty: This template has no connections yet.
wbConnNormalHelp: Moves forward to the next step for one business result; does not count rework.
wbConnLoopHelp: Returns to an earlier step to redo work; counts toward rework rounds.
wbConnRetryHelp: The system automatically re-sends the same step — a technical retry that consumes no rework rounds.
wbConnMissingEdges: These business results are declared but have no destination yet (fill in per the template definition; do not delete connections):
wbConnCountBreakdown: {normal} normal routing · {loop} business loop · {retry} call retry
wbConnLegendLoopHelp: Returns to an earlier step via a business result; counts toward rework rounds.
wbConnLegendRetryHelp: The system re-sends the same step; consumes no rework rounds.
wbConnLegendRoundsHelp: The workflow-level round cap (the "Max rounds" setting in the right panel); it is a different concept from the two above.
wbSecBasicNote: what this step does, who does it, what it delivers
wbSecOutcomeNote: how completion is judged and where it goes next
wbSecAdvancedNote: technical id, AI service and model, data structure
wbAdvancedHelp: Implementation details you can normally ignore: node id, AI service, and the structure of delivered data. The Basics and Result & destination sections above are enough for everyday configuration.
wbOutgoingHelp: Every connection leaving this step, and which category each one belongs to.
wbOutgoingNone: This step has no destination yet — it ends when done.
wbFanoutGroupHelp: The same step runs in parallel over the source list; each sub-task delivers its own report, and aggregation happens only after all of them finish.
wbFanoutSummaryWait: While any sub-task is unfinished, the next step (aggregation) stays waiting rather than showing as complete.
wbBuiltinStructureReadonly: A built-in template's steps and connections are read-only. To change them, use "Save as" to copy it into your own template; providers and models are configured in the library's "Model override".
wbBuiltinSaveDisabled: A built-in template cannot be overwritten. Use "Save as" to keep your changes.
wbModelScopeNote: Default / override / reset apply to built-in templates only, via "Model override" on the template row in the library.
wbAgentHelp: The AI service that runs this step; usually no change needed.
wbUnsavedDesc: Choose how to handle these changes before closing the workspace.
